subject: reading
title: The Cat Nap
about: A boy and his sleepy cat. Practises short a, i, e and u words with ck, ng, ch, th and double letters (black, ring, chin, then, bell), plus the tricky words the, a, is, what and of. Decodable at CKLA Unit 1, so he can read it alone.
tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again with expression on the Ring, ring, ring line.

passage.text:
Sam has a big black cat.
The cat is Max.

Max naps on the mat.
Max naps on the bed.

Sam hops up.
"Get up, Max!"
Max just naps.

Sam gets a bell.
Ring, ring, ring!
Max lifts his chin.
Then Max naps on Sam's lap.

Sam grins.
"What a lot of naps!"
Sam naps with Max.

cards.q: Who has a big black cat?
cards.note: The first line says Sam has a big black cat.

cards.q: What is the name of the cat?
cards.note: The cat is Max; Sam is the boy.

cards.q: What does Sam get to wake up Max?
cards.note: Sam gets a bell and rings it three times.

cards.q: What does Max do when the bell rings?
cards.note: Max only lifts his chin, then naps again on Sam's lap.
Max naps on the mat, then the bed, then Sam's lap: ask him to retell the order.

cards.q: What happens at the end of the story?
cards.note: The last line is Sam naps with Max.

cards.q: How does Sam feel when Max naps on his lap?
cards.note: Sam grins, so he is glad.

cards.q: Why does Sam ring the bell?
cards.note: Sam wants Max to get up, so he rings a bell.

cards.q: What does the word nap mean?
cards.note: A nap is a short sleep in the daytime.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Sam gets a bell; belt and bill are look-alikes that are not in the story.
